title: Autonomous Execution for Multi-GPU Systems: Compiler Support
problem: Current high-level frameworks and compilers lack support for constructs enabling autonomous GPU execution and GPU-initiated multi-GPU communication. Existing systems do not provide abstractions for kernels to independently organize execution and move data across devices.
motivation: As HPC systems increasingly use GPUs as autonomous execution units with independent communication capabilities, compiler support is essential for developers to efficiently write GPU-first code that exploits device-to-device communication and reduces latency.
method: The system's code generator combines multiple GPU operations into persistent kernels—GPU programs designed to stay running and coordinate their execution without waiting for the CPU. These kernels use NVSHMEM (a library enabling GPU-to-GPU communication) to transfer data between devices directly. Accessible through Python, this lets multi-GPU systems execute autonomously, with GPUs independently organizing their computation and data flow.
key_novelty: The innovation is compiler support enabling autonomous multi-GPU execution, where GPUs independently manage their own computation and data transfers.
contributions: Code generator for efficient fusion and scheduling of persistent kernels enabling autonomous execution
High-level abstractions over GPU device resources for productive GPU-first programming
Integration of NVSHMEM-based GPU-initiated communication within Python code
Evaluation on 22 NPBench kernels with 6.1x-30.8x speedups and 98% scaling efficiency

metrics.speedup: 6.1x over DaCe, 30.8x over cuNumeric on 8 GPUs (3D Jacobi)

primary_theme: Compiler support for autonomous multi-GPU execution
